correctness.rationale: The invertible linear map y_j=j(x_j-x_{j+1}) sends the constant-density ordered chamber to the uniform simplex. In the first m-1 coordinates the divergence of the coefficient field y_i(delta_{iℓ}-y_ℓ) is 1-m y_i; its flux vanishes on coordinate faces and on y_m=0 (the sum of its components is y_i y_m). Integration by parts and pairing i,j therefore give the claimed covariance identity with factor 1/m. The two-coordinate transfer criterion orders the gradient of F on the strict chamber. The prefix means b_i-b_j for i<j are (1/(ij)) times the sum of all g_k-g_ℓ for k≤i<ℓ≤j, so they are nonnegative. Equality forces every tangential derivative of f to vanish throughout the interior, hence constancy by connectedness, continuity and symmetry. For p>1, the positive-part p-power supplies a C¹ extension. For entropy the smoothed differences are sums of positive log ratios that increase as epsilon decreases; uniform convergence on the simplex and monotone convergence in the identity give strictly positive covariance for negative entropy. At m=2, E[M H]=7/24+log(2)/12, E[M]=3/4 and E[H]=1/2, giving exactly the claimed covariance.
residual_risks: The polynomial checks in the frozen record are corroboration only; the proof depends on uniform Dirichlet parameters, and the smooth equality argument is restricted to the stated regularity and symmetry.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The sign also has a route through standard association after passing to cumulative gaps: they are uniform order statistics, and ranked partial sums increase in them. No originality is attributed to the underlying association or integration-by-parts machinery.

originality.rationale: Credit the strict all-statistics covariance law and its positive-pair identity, not the already-known largest-spacing/Greenwood covariance or the ranked-gap substitution itself. The closest exact records share the quadratic special case and in one case the same coordinates, but do not cover general symmetric Schur-convex statistics. No inspected primary theorem implies the credited claim.
residual_risks: A stronger prior majorization association result or a prior formulation of the same Dirichlet gradient identity could narrow credit; the literature search is not a priority proof.

value.rationale: A single inequality with a sharp equality condition treats simultaneous dependence of the maximum with all admitted dispersion scores, including nonseparable ones; entropy and power sums illustrate why a one-statistic formula does not settle this question. The positive-pair representation explains the sign and strictness, rather than just computing selected moments.
residual_risks: No credit for an unequal-parameter law, a correlation rate, or a general stochastic domination theorem.
